red_flags: extreme cyclicality once AI-driven NAND shortage normalizes
91.6% ROE/56.5% margin are cycle-peak, not sustainable run-rate
SNDK.one_line: NAND flash memory maker riding an AI-driven datacenter storage shortage with bits on allocation into 2027.
SNDK.reason: FY26 revenue +175% YoY, datacenter rev +437%; management sees NAND market $300B->$500B (CY26->CY27) with bits on allocation beyond 2027. NTM P/E just 7.9x vs trailing 24.1x shows the market has not fully priced the multi-year shortage; v1 flagged 'excessive' likely off trailing multiple/momentum, not forward allocation dynamics. Worth full diligence on cycle duration/downside if AI capex slows.

red_flags: low FCF yield (0.9%) vs heavy capex
cyclical HDD demand if hyperscaler capex decelerates
STX.one_line: Nearline HDD maker sold out through 2026 with visibility into 2027 as AI data centers buy all available capacity.
STX.reason: Q4 FY26 non-GAAP EPS $5.71 vs $5.10 consensus, record gross margins; nearline pricing targeted $25-30/TB. NTM P/E 22.6x vs trailing 66.1x shows earnings catching up to price. Genuine multi-year demand visibility (2027 agreements) supports advancing past a quick screen despite the stock's big 12-month run.

red_flags: margin/ROE (72.9%/130.9%) look inflated by post-spinoff accounting - verify normalized figures
low FCF yield (1.4%)
WDC.one_line: Pure-play nearline HDD maker, capacity fully allocated through CY2026 on AI storage demand, highest Street upside of the storage trio.
WDC.reason: Nearline capacity fully allocated through 2026 with long-term hyperscaler agreements into 2027; consumer HDD prices up ~50% in 5 months. Street upside 45.6% is the largest in the group. Reported margin/ROE look distorted by the SanDisk spin-off equity base and need verification in full diligence, but the core pricing-power thesis is sound.

red_flags: dividend cut 50% (2025) amid prolonged chemicals downturn
negative TTM margin/ROE
debt-to-equity >100%, net debt/EBITDA 3.8x
tariff uncertainty
DOW.one_line: Commodity chemicals major mid-downturn: dividend already halved, balance sheet stretched, oversupply persists.
DOW.reason: Bottom-of-cycle industry conditions persist into 2026 per management; ~$14B liquidity and no maturities until 2029 avert a solvency crisis, but the 2025 dividend cut plus negative trailing profitability are disqualifying red flags for a quick pass. Cheap NTM P/E (14.6x) reflects trough earnings, not a clear bargain yet.

red_flags: 12-month momentum -20.5%, confirm nothing structural behind the pullback
CRH.one_line: Largest US-focused building materials/aggregates group; scaled, vertically integrated, and pulled back despite steady fundamentals.
CRH.reason: Analysts (24 covering) see 56.6% upside, an outlier versus peers VMC/MLM (~30%), while trading at just 13.4x NTM P/E with 15.8% ROE and positive FCF yield. Combined with a 20% share pullback, this looks like a case a pure statistical rank could miss; worth confirming why Street upside is so much wider than peers before advancing capital.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of CRH's North American aggregates/materials scale)

red_flags: ROE (8.9%) low relative to 36.7% operating margin - capital-intensive asset base
momentum -17.4%
MLM.one_line: Aggregates/quarry leader with irreplaceable local reserve positions; raised FY26 revenue guide to $7.2-7.4B.
MLM.reason: Record aggregates revenue ($1.5B/qtr) on 4th straight quarter of shipment growth; pricing trending toward the low end of guide on mix/acquisitions but volumes toward the high end. Rich 24x NTM multiple is broadly justified by the quarry-scarcity moat and guidance raise.

red_flags: organic volume growth soft (1-3% guided; revenue growth in data card only 2.5%)
momentum -11.7%
VMC.one_line: Largest US aggregates producer; pricing-led growth (4-6% guided) as infrastructure/public demand offsets soft private volumes.
VMC.reason: FY26 EBITDA guide $2.4-2.6B with mix-adjusted pricing +5%. Growth is price-led rather than volume-led right now, and the 24x NTM multiple leaves limited room for volume disappointment, but the oligopoly moat and infrastructure-spend tailwind support a full look.

red_flags: Grasberg still recovering from Sept-2025 mud rush - only ~65% of nameplate capacity in H2 2026, full recovery not until late 2027
2026 sales guidance already cut once
FCX.one_line: Copper/gold major whose flagship Grasberg mine remains disrupted; upside already priced in with only 0.2% Street upside left.
FCX.reason: Strong copper ($6.00/lb) and gold ($4,500/oz) price assumptions support cash flow (~$8.7B ops CF guided), but Grasberg's slow ramp pushes real volume recovery to 2027-2028 and the stock has already re-rated (+95% momentum) on recovery hopes, leaving almost no analyst upside. Better as a 2027 re-entry watch than an immediate advance.

red_flags: revenue declining YoY (-1.2%)
crop protection pricing down 4% in Q2
pending Biosciences spin-off creates near-term execution/dis-synergy uncertainty
CTVA.one_line: Seed/crop-protection leader guiding only ~7% EPS growth amid soft farmer margins, mid-separation into two companies.
CTVA.reason: Management reaffirmed 2026 EBITDA of $4.0-4.2B (margins 22-23%) but crop protection net sales fell YoY on price and volume; overall ag environment described as 'mixed' with pressured farmer margins. The 4Q26 Biosciences separation could unlock value later but adds near-term uncertainty, so this does not clear the bar today - worth revisiting post-separation.

red_flags: Q1 2026 net loss of $258M
negative FCF yield (-10.2%)
net debt/EBITDA 3.4x
sulfur cost spike (~$1,200/ton) pushing much of the producer cost curve underwater per CEO
MOS.one_line: Potash/phosphate producer squeezed between soft crop-nutrient pricing and a sulfur cost spike; posting losses.
MOS.reason: Reported an actual net loss and negative free cash flow last quarter; management's own commentary flags industry-wide cost-curve stress from sulfur prices. Clear disqualifying red flags (negative earnings/FCF, elevated leverage) despite a supportive long-run potash demand story (Canpotex record shipments).

red_flags: earnings/cash flow entirely dependent on gold price staying elevated
NEM.one_line: World's largest gold miner posting record free cash flow as gold trades above $4,400/oz, with a net-cash balance sheet.
NEM.reason: Record FCF ($3.1B Q1, $2.2B Q2 2026) with AISC guided ~$1,680/oz against realized prices near $4,900/oz - a huge cash margin. Net debt/EBITDA is negative (net cash), ROE 25.9%, and NTM P/E of just 12.2x looks too cheap for record-margin cash generation even with a moderate Street upside (12.5%). v1's 'fair' call undersells the margin structure at current gold prices.

red_flags: two rounds of large impairments (Dec-25, and $2.9B pre-tax in FY26 Q3) on failed green-hydrogen megaprojects - capital-allocation credibility hit
GAAP loss per share in the impairment quarter
APD.one_line: Industrial-gas major that just wrote off ~$2.9B of green-hydrogen megaprojects and refocused on core industrial gas plus a $3B traditional pipeline.
APD.reason: Core industrial gas segment delivered 25.6% operating margin and beat its own guidance even in the impairment quarter; management raised full-year adjusted EPS guide to $13.39-$13.49 (+11-12%). The write-offs are a real governance red flag worth probing in full diligence, but they de-risk forward capex and the core moat/oligopoly economics are intact at a reasonable 19.5x NTM multiple.

red_flags: premium 26x NTM multiple leaves little margin for execution slips
LIN.one_line: Largest global industrial-gas company; best-in-class oligopoly with a secured, contracted project backlog.
LIN.reason: Consistent double-digit EPS growth (26.2% NTM), low leverage (1.7x net debt/EBITDA), and a durable moat from on-site/pipeline gas contracts that are effectively impossible to replicate. Multiple is rich but broadly fair given the quality and growth on offer; no red flags found.

red_flags: thin GAAP margin (6.6%) typical of the packaging industry
net debt/EBITDA 3.4x
BALL.one_line: Aluminum can maker benefiting from sustainability-driven substitution away from plastic, cheap on a forward basis.
BALL.reason: 29.6% forward EPS growth and 19.7% revenue growth against a cheap 12.9x NTM multiple and 27.7% Street upside. Leverage is a watch item but not disqualifying given positive, improving FCF generation.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of Ball's can substitution thesis)

red_flags: net debt/EBITDA 4.0x post Berry Global merger - integration and de-leveraging execution risk
high 6.2% dividend yield versus thin GAAP margin - confirm coverage
AMCR.one_line: Flexible/rigid packaging major, enlarged by the 2025 Berry Global merger, still working through integration and de-leveraging.
AMCR.reason: 83% forward EPS growth reflects merger synergy ramp; FCF yield 7.7% is strong and should fund de-leveraging from the elevated 4.0x net debt/EBITDA. Cheap 10.0x NTM multiple for the combined entity's growth, but leverage and integration execution are real items to verify in full diligence.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of Amcor-Berry Global merger, closed 2025)

AVY.one_line: Pressure-sensitive labeling/packaging materials leader with strong ROE and FCF generation.
AVY.reason: 31.2% ROE and 7.7% FCF yield are well above packaging-sector norms, at a reasonable 15.6x NTM multiple with 18.5% Street upside. No red flags identified in the data card; standard label-demand cyclicality is the main watch item.

red_flags: negative TTM margin (-14.2%) and ROE (-16.5%)
Wells Fargo flags margin compression / moderating volumes in corrugated packaging during DS Smith integration
GAAP unprofitable currently
IP.one_line: Containerboard major mid-integration of the DS Smith combination; management targets $6B 2027 EBITDA (vs $3.5-3.7B 2026) but currently unprofitable on a GAAP basis.
IP.reason: The 2027 synergy targets ($600-700M) and turnaround math are attractive and the 36.8% Street upside/8.9% FCF yield hint at deep value, but current negative margin/ROE is a real red flag until integration proof-points show up in reported numbers. Best treated as a 2027 re-rating watch item rather than an immediate advance.

red_flags: Street upside modest (9.3%) - much of the cycle recovery may already be priced in
FCF yield low (2.0%) on heavy new-mill capex
PKG.one_line: Best-in-class containerboard/corrugated operator with consistently disciplined execution through the packaging cycle.
PKG.reason: 75.5% forward EPS growth reflects genuine cycle recovery/price increases, at a fair-not-cheap 19.1x NTM multiple. Consistently one of the highest-quality operators in the sub-industry; limited Street upside suggests the market has already recognized this.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of PKG's operating track record)

red_flags: margin still thin mid-integration (1.6%) and ROE weak (2.7%) - confirm synergy delivery is on track
flat revenue growth (1.1%)
SW.one_line: Global containerboard scale leader formed by the 2024 Smurfit Kappa/WestRock merger, still ramping merger synergies.
SW.reason: Trailing P/E of 49.4x vs NTM 15.4x signals the market expects a large earnings step-up as synergies (~$400M targeted) and 2026 price increases land. Cheap if delivered, but current margin/ROE weakness means integration execution needs verification in full diligence.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of Smurfit Westrock merger, closed July 2024)

red_flags: single-commodity (lithium) price exposure remains highly volatile
trailing GAAP P/E (406x) reflects a near-zero prior-year earnings base, not a red flag itself but a data-quality caution
ALB.one_line: Largest global lithium producer, riding a 2026 lithium-price recovery with EBITDA more than doubling YoY.
ALB.reason: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin hit 49% (net sales +31% YoY), EPS beat consensus by ~24%; FCF yield 10.3% and net debt/EBITDA just 0.2x show a strong balance sheet through the trough. 9.7x NTM P/E and 56.4% Street upside suggest the market/model may be over-anchored on the distorted trailing multiple rather than the recovery already underway - v1's 'excessive' tag looks like exactly this artifact.

red_flags: premium valuation (30.8x NTM) leaves little room for a demand or margin miss
ECL.one_line: Water treatment/hygiene leader with a service-and-switching-cost moat; consistent double-digit growth.
ECL.reason: 26.6% forward EPS growth and 22% ROE at a rich-but-justified multiple given the recurring, mission-critical nature of Ecolab's services across food, water and industrial customers. No disqualifying red flags; this is a quality compounder priced for quality.

red_flags: negative TTM margin (2.6%) and ROE (-5.5%)
negative FCF yield (-7.9%)
historically over-levered post DuPont N&B merger, still delevering
guided sales growth only 2-4%
IFF.one_line: Flavors/fragrances major mid-transformation, divesting Food Ingredients to cut debt and stranded costs, but growth is currently modest.
IFF.reason: The divestiture (targeting 2.0-2.5x net debt/EBITDA vs 4.5x historically) and stranded-cost removal are real positives, and H1 2026 FCF improved materially ($378M, +$284M YoY), but the data card's negative trailing margin/ROE/FCF and only 2-4% guided growth mean price is not clearly cheap relative to plausible growth today. Revisit after the divestiture closes and leverage comes down.

red_flags: negative TTM margin (-1.1%) and ROE (-2.3%)
net debt/EBITDA 3.3x
6.8% dividend yield needs coverage verification given still-negative trailing earnings
LYB.one_line: Commodity petrochemicals major mid-cycle-trough, exiting refining and divesting European assets while cutting costs.
LYB.reason: Q2 2026 turned net-income positive ($0.6B GAAP, $1.4B excluding items) after the Houston refinery exit and European O&P divestiture (completing 2026), with a $1.3B cost program. NTM P/E of 8.3x is statistically cheap and FCF yield 6.5% is solid, but the trailing profitability is still negative and self-help isn't fully proven yet - a name to revisit once the divestiture and cost program are fully delivered.

red_flags: organic growth has been sluggish; confirm portfolio-pruning progress in diligence
PPG.one_line: Global paints/coatings major with a good brand/distribution moat, trading cheap relative to its margin and ROE profile.
PPG.reason: 19.3% ROE and 4.6% FCF yield at just 12.7x NTM P/E look statistically cheap for a coatings oligopoly member; the business has been under activist and new-CEO pressure to sharpen the portfolio, which could be a re-rating catalyst worth verifying in full diligence.
sources: triage_cards.csv (general knowledge of PPG activist involvement/portfolio review)

red_flags: net debt/EBITDA 3.1x, elevated partly from buyback funding - confirm this stays disciplined
SHW.one_line: Paint/coatings category leader with the best store-network and contractor-relationship moat in the sub-industry.
SHW.reason: 65.1% ROE is exceptional even for a high-quality compounder; 25.6% forward EPS growth at 24.9x NTM P/E is a fair price for one of the highest-quality franchises in Materials. No disqualifying red flags.

red_flags: tariff-dependent pricing - a trade-policy reversal is a real risk to monitor
low FCF yield (1.2%) on heavy capex
NUE.one_line: Largest US steelmaker; tariffs are driving record shipments and 2027 contracts already being written at $1,100-1,175/ton vs ~$800 in 2026.
NUE.reason: Q3 guide of $5.55-5.65 EPS, up from $5.04 in Q2, with steel-mill shipments guided +10% YoY on infrastructure/data-center/energy demand. NTM P/E of just 12.6x for this earnings trajectory looks cheap even after the stock's big run; v1's 'excessive' tag likely reflects trailing momentum rather than the forward tariff-supported pricing backdrop, so worth a full look with tariff-durability risk flagged.

red_flags: tariff-dependent pricing - a trade-policy reversal is a real risk to monitor
low FCF yield (0.7%) on heavy capex
STLD.one_line: Efficient EAF steel/aluminum producer guiding record shipments, benefiting from the same tariff-driven pricing cycle as Nucor.
STLD.reason: Q3 guide of $5.34-5.38 EPS on record steel shipments plus growing aluminum contribution. 12.3x NTM P/E is cheap for the earnings trajectory described; same tariff-durability caveat as Nucor applies, but the low-cost operating model and diversification into aluminum support a full diligence pass.

red_flags: net debt/EBITDA 5.7x is high even for a REIT - confirm coverage from contracted backlog
raw P/E (62x) is GAAP/depreciation-distorted; use FFO-based multiple in full diligence
DLR.one_line: Largest data-center REIT by footprint, with a record $1.9B signed-not-yet-commenced lease backlog and $20B under construction for AI/hyperscale demand.
DLR.reason: Using the cost-of-capital-minus-FCF-yield heuristic (~9%-5.6%=~3.4% required growth), actual revenue growth of 29.9% and a raised outlook clear that bar comfortably despite the headline P/E looking rich on a GAAP basis. Leverage is the main item to verify against contracted, investment-grade tenant backlog in full diligence.

red_flags: net debt/EBITDA 4.9x amid a $4-5B/year capex plan to double capacity through 2029 - funding/dilution risk to verify
EQIX.one_line: Interconnection-density leader among data-center REITs; raised guidance again in 2026 on hyperscaler/AI demand.
EQIX.reason: Required growth under the FCF-yield heuristic (~9%-3.8%=~5.2%) is well below Equinix's actual mid-teens-to-20% growth trajectory, so the rich headline P/E (54.7x, GAAP/depreciation-distorted) is less alarming than it looks. The network-effect moat (270+ interconnected facilities) is arguably the hardest to replicate among data-center REITs; funding the capacity-doubling capex plan is the key diligence item.

red_flags: headline GAAP P/E (160x) is misleading - real FFO multiple is roughly 12x on guided $1.73-1.77 FFO/share; use FFO in diligence
life-science segment has faced sector-wide oversupply - confirm Healthpeak's exposure
DOC.one_line: Diversified health-care REIT (outpatient medical, life science, senior housing) that just raised FY26 FFO guidance on senior-housing strength.
DOC.reason: Senior Housing same-store NOI +19.2% and FY26 AFFO guidance raised to $1.73-1.77/share after a beat-and-raise Q2; on that FFO basis the ~12x multiple looks cheap versus growth, very different from the GAAP-distorted 160x P/E in the data card. Life science segment softness is the main offsetting risk to verify.

red_flags: headline GAAP P/E (124x) is misleading - use FFO multiple (roughly mid-20s) in diligence
net debt/EBITDA 5.3x
VTR.one_line: Second-largest global senior-housing REIT owner, benefiting from supply-constrained senior housing and aging demographics.
VTR.reason: 21.7% revenue growth and accelerating occupancy/NOI in senior housing (900+ properties) support the growth case; low 2.3% dividend yield signals room for payout growth rather than a covered-out REIT. On an FFO basis the multiple is moderate, not the extreme headline GAAP P/E in the data card.
